{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify premises
assert (df['status'] == 'completed').sum() + (df['status'] == 'refunded').sum() == len(df), "Status column has unexpected values"
assert df['revenue'].str.contains(',').any(), "Revenue should contain commas as per documentation"

# Filter completed orders
completed = df[df['status'] == 'completed']

# Convert revenue: remove commas and cast to float
completed['revenue_clean'] = completed['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Identify QA orders (revenue = 999999.99)
qa_mask = completed['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99
n_qa = qa_mask.sum()

# Check: are QA orders part of 'completed'? Yes, they are.
# But are they real orders? No. They are internal test entries.
# The contract says 'all completed orders', but if we include them,
# the mean revenue becomes 7393.76, which is dominated by 6 entries
# of 999999.99 — an artifact, not a business signal.

# Compute mean with and without QA
mean_with_qa = completed['revenue_clean'].mean()
completed_no_qa = completed[~qa_mask]
mean_without_qa = completed_no_qa['revenue_clean'].mean()

# Print results
print(f"Number of completed orders: {len(completed)}")
print(f"Number of QA orders in completed set: {n_qa}")
print(f"Mean revenue including QA: {mean_with_qa:.2f}")
print(f"Mean revenue excluding QA: {mean_without_qa:.2f}")"}
